notes: Body initializes the caller-provided 32-bit output to -1, checks context status ID 0 for value 4, lazily initializes the backing object, retrieves float attribute ID 0x28, converts it with signed float-to-int conversion, and stores the 32-bit integer. The proposal incorrectly says player attribute and float return: this routine writes an integer through an output pointer. No direct lifted callers are indexed or found; helper behavior is consistent with the context status and float attribute accessors.

Body reads the context record's ID 0 value, evaluates the context metric, and computes metric minus the record's low byte. It returns a bucketed encoding: deltas 0..4 pass through, deltas above 4 return 5, deltas -1..-4 map to 6..9, and lower deltas map to 10. Thus this is not simply a delta-returning routine. No direct lifted callers are indexed or found; the named record accessor and metric evaluator support the operand interpretation.

The body queries context status IDs 0x13, 0, and 0x18 and returns one only when their low-byte results equal 4, 8, and 2, respectively. Caller stores the returned predicate into a context result byte before invoking the next status predicate, consistent with a boolean helper.

The body requires status ID 1 minus 0x87 to be at most 0x12, then requires status ID 2 minus 0x87 to be below 0x13. Both are therefore in the inclusive range 0x87..0x99. The proposal name omits the second required status check, and its evidence incorrectly allowed ID 2 through 0x9a. The caller uses this combined predicate in a larger conditional before querying status ID 0x4e.

The body queries status ID 0x48 and returns true only when its signed comparison against zero is greater than zero; zero and negative values return false. The proposed nonzero name would incorrectly include negative values. Callers consume the result as a boolean predicate/context result.
